name: Fennel
grown_as: Bronze fennel, Foeniculum vulgare 'Purpureum': herb fennel, a long-lived perennial grown for its leaves and seed (not Florence fennel, the bulb vegetable, which is an annual). Its feathery foliage is bronze-purple, greening a little with age.
habit: A tall clump of several upright stems 1.5 to 2.5 m high and about 60 cm across, branching widely above, from a thick root. Stems smooth, glossy, finely striped, blue-green, solid with white pith when young. Strong aniseed smell.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate up the stems; large leaves at the base in spring
leaf.type: Compound, three or four times pinnate, cut into hair-fine thread-like segments
leaf.outline: Triangular overall, up to 30 cm or more, the threads pointing in all directions so the leaf is a soft three-dimensional plume, not flat
leaf.base: A long conspicuous sheath, several cm, wrapping the stem
leaf.tip: Each thread ends in a fine point
leaf.margin: No teeth: threads 1 to 5 cm long (longer than dill's), very narrow
leaf.colour: Bronze-purple when young, ageing to bronze-green

flower.form: Flat to slightly domed compound umbels of tiny flowers
flower.petals: Five tiny yellow petals per flower, tips turned inwards
flower.centre: Yellow stamens and a swollen yellow base to the styles
flower.carried: On long stalks at the ends of stems and branches, facing up; each umbel 4 to 8 cm across with 12 to 25 rays, many umbels open together
flower.size: Flowers 1 to 2 mm; umbels 4 to 8 cm

fruit: Oblong seeds 4 to 6 mm long, in pairs, with five strong pale ribs and no wing. Green ripening to grey-brown. Umbels of seed stand into winter.
seedling: Two long narrow seed leaves, then first true leaves divided into threads
winter: Dies down to the ground. Dead hollow brown stems often stand with their seed umbels. Fresh feathery shoots appear at the crown from late winter.

leaf: hair-fine threads spreading in all directions, a soft plume
bloom: yellow umbel of many rays, no bracts
tiny yellow flowers in small umbels at the ray tips
seed: oblong ribbed seed with strong pale ribs
young: a clump of feathery bronze plumes from the ground
crop: a dense clump of tall feathery bronze foliage
flower: tall branched stems over 1.5 m with many yellow umbels
seedhead: umbels of ribbed grey-brown seeds on stiff rays
dormant: dead brown stems standing, some with seed umbels
small feathery bronze-purple new shoots at the base

look_alikes: Dill is an annual with one stem, flatter leaves and flat winged seeds. Florence fennel has a swollen white bulb at the base. Hemlock and other white umbellifers have flat, divided but not thread-like leaflets and white flowers.
